Large Language Models (LLMs) are like this smart friend. LLMs are computer programs that can understand and create human language. They learn from a lot of text, like books and websites. But they only know what they learned during their training.

If you ask an LLM about very new information, or specific details not in its training, it might guess wrong. It might even make up information. This is called "hallucination."

RAG solves this problem. It helps LLMs get new and correct information to answer questions.

It gives the LLM **new information**. This information is always fresh and up-to-date.

It makes the LLM's answers **more correct**. It helps the LLM not make things up.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG, helps this smart friend. RAG gives the LLM new, correct information. This helps the LLM give better answers.
